when: block completed less than 3 years ago
summary: Bathroom/toilet wall and floor finishes in a newly built block cannot be removed or replaced for 3 years from the block's completion date (protects the waterproofing membrane).
alternative: Overlay new floor finishes on the existing ones with adhesive (see HDB-BATH-3YR-OVERLAY).
quote: The toilet floor and wall finishes provided by HDB/ developer must not be replaced for a period of 3 years from the completion date of the block for this reason.

when: any time, including the first 3 years
summary: New bathroom floor finishes may be laid over the existing ones using adhesive, also during the 3-year restriction.
conditions: Only 1 existing layer of floor finishes (including cement screed)
New finish including adhesive at most 13mm thick
No tampering with the floor trap
No backflow or lateral seepage into the bedroom
quote: You can, however, lay new toilet floor finishes over the existing floor finishes using adhesives.

when: block completed 3 or more years ago
summary: Replacing bathroom/toilet floor finishes after the first 3 years needs an HDB permit and a new waterproofing system.
conditions: Total thickness of finishes and screed at most 50mm
Pre-packed waterproofing screed and waterproofing membrane before the new finishes
Membrane upturned at least 150mm against walls, kerbs and pipes
UPVC floor trap grating with long collar
Water test after replacing the floor finishes
quote: Replacement of existing bathroom/ toilet floor finishes after first 3 years from the date of completion of the block. | Yes | Total thickness of finishes and screed must not exceed 50mm

when: block completed 3 or more years ago
summary: Replacing bathroom/toilet wall finishes after the first 3 years needs an HDB permit.
conditions: No tampering with existing structures
Total thickness of wall finishes including plaster at most 25mm
quote: Replacement of existing bathroom/ toilet wall finishes after first 3 years from the date of completion of the block | Yes

when: hacking out and replacing existing floor finishes (ceramic, homogeneous, terrazzo, marble, parquet/timber, other tiles)
summary: Replacing existing floor finishes needs an HDB permit.
conditions: Total thickness of floor finishes and screed at most 50mm
Wet areas: pre-packed waterproofing screed; membrane upturned at least 150mm in bathrooms, and around sanitary stacks (400mm radius) in kitchen/open balcony
UPVC floor trap grating with long collar
Pre-packed screed in dry areas
Gas pipes must not be embedded in the screed or finishes
alternative: Overlay with adhesive (HDB-FLOOR-OVERLAY) or vinyl (HDB-FLOOR-VINYL) needs no permit.
quote: Replacement of floor finishes: Ceramic / Homogeneous / Terrazzo / Marble / Parquet/ timber / Other tiles | Yes | Total thickness of floor finishes and screed must not exceed 50mm

when: laying over existing floor finishes with adhesive only
summary: Laying a floor finish over the existing one with adhesive only needs no permit.
conditions: Only 1 existing layer of floor finishes (including cement screed)
New finish including adhesive at most 13mm thick
No tampering with the floor trap
No backflow or lateral seepage into the bedroom
quote: Laying of floor finishes over existing floor finishes using adhesive only | No | There should be only 1 layer of existing floor finishes including cement screed before proceeding to lay the additional layer of floor finishes

when: always
summary: Laying vinyl, carpet or linoleum needs no permit.
quote: Laying of vinyl finishes/ carpet/ linoleum | No | Not applicable

when: laying parquet/timber/laminate/bamboo over existing finishes
summary: Laying or replacing parquet/timber (laminated, bamboo) flooring needs no permit when it goes over the existing finishes without a platform, cement screed or hacking.
conditions: No raising the floor as a platform
No cement screed
No hacking/removal of existing floor finishes
Flats without existing finishes: finishes and screed at most 50mm
quote: Laying/ replacement of parquet/ timber flooring (also known as laminated or bamboo flooring) | No | The laying of flooring over existing finishes should not involve the following: Raising the floor as a platform / Usage of cement screed / Hacking/ removal of existing floor finishes

when: raising the floor level
summary: Raising the floor level with concrete beyond 50mm (including finishes) is not allowed; topping up with lightweight screed in a balcony, kitchen or bathroom needs a permit.
conditions: Lightweight top-up: non-combustible in-fill, existing finishes and screed removed, total load at most 120kg/m2, parapet/window sill at least 1000mm above the finished floor
alternative: Topping up with lightweight screed/block (permit) or an overlay within the thickness limits.
quote: Raising of floor level exceeding the allowed thickness of 50mm (inclusive of floor finishes) using concrete

when: laying wall finishes over existing wall finishes with adhesive
summary: Laying new wall finishes over existing ones with adhesive needs no permit.
conditions: No tampering with existing structures and wall finishes
New wall finish at most 13mm thick
No third layer of wall finishes
quote: Laying of wall finishes over existing wall finishes using adhesives | No | No tampering of existing structures and wall finishes / The thickness of the wall finishes used must not exceed 13mm

when: replacing internal wall finishes (outside bathrooms)
summary: Replacing internal wall finishes up to ceiling level needs a permit.
conditions: No tampering with existing structures
Total thickness of wall finishes including plaster at most 25mm
RC wall surface must not be hacked to form a key for tiling (use spatterdash)
alternative: Overlay with adhesive (HDB-WALLFIN-OVERLAY) needs no permit.
quote: Replacement of internal wall finishes up to ceiling level | Yes | No tampering of existing structures / Total thickness of the wall finishes, including plaster, must not exceed 25mm

when: inside the flat
summary: Wallpaper, plastering, rock-stone finish and spray painting inside the flat need no permit; painting the outside of the building is not allowed.
conditions: Pre-packed material for plastering
Do not paint external parts of the building (e.g. common corridor walls and ceilings)
Household shelter: do not paint over the HS door notice, locking bolts or door seal
quote: Wallpaper, cement and sand plastering, gypsum plastering, rock-stone finish, spray painting | No | Pre-packed material must be used for plastering

when: demolishing or altering a non-structural partition wall (hollow block/brick, drywall, Ferrolite) or non-load-bearing RC element
summary: All demolition or alteration of walls needs HDB's prior written approval.
conditions: Existing RC structures must not be tampered with
Demolition only up to the underside of the RC beam/slab
Brick/block walls demolished top down; drywall/Ferrolite in full, joint to joint
Stop and inform HDB immediately if steel bars are found
Non-load-bearing RC elements: a Professional Engineer (Civil/Structural) must supervise
Noisy works only Mon-Fri 9am-5pm, at most 3 consecutive days
quote: All demolition or alteration of walls can only be carried out after obtaining HDB’s approval

when: the wall is structural (RC wall, column, beam, slab) or the change cuts a new doorway through an RC wall
summary: Hacking or removing structural members (RC walls, columns, beams, slabs, maisonette staircases) is not allowed, nor is a new entrance through an RC wall.
alternative: Keep the RC wall; change only non-structural partitions (with a permit).
quote: Hacking and removal of structural members such as reinforced concrete wall, columns, beams, slabs, and staircases within executive maisonettes, etc.

when: building a new partition (63mm hollow block, 80mm glass block or gypsum)
summary: Erecting a 63mm hollow block, 80mm glass block or gypsum partition needs no permit; combustible or toxic partitions are not allowed.
conditions: Adequate natural lighting and ventilation if it creates a habitable room
Fire escape route direct, not through another room
RC lintol over any opening in a hollow block wall
Only one layer of 63mm hollow block or 80mm glass block
Fasteners at most 6mm diameter and 40mm penetration
No partitions of combustible or toxic-emission materials (e.g. plywood, plastics, asbestos)
quote: Erection of 63mm thick hollow block wall | No | Adequate natural lighting and ventilation must be provided if creating a room for habitation

when: installing false ceilings, cornices or pelmets in the flat
summary: False ceilings, cornices and pelmets need no permit, subject to clearance, material and fixing limits.
conditions: False ceiling at least 2.4m above finished floor level (not applicable to toilets and bathrooms)
Pelmet at least 2.10m above finished floor level
Non-combustible materials only
No gas pipe enclosed in the false ceiling
Fasteners at most 6mm diameter and 40mm penetration into the RC slab
Owner removes and reinstates it for inspection and maintenance
Plastering of ceilings is not allowed
No cornices inside the household shelter
Topmost floor with pitched roof: keep the original roof ceiling, 600x600mm access opening
quote: For installation of false ceilings, the minimum clearance height of 2.4 metres measured from finished floor level (not applicable for toilets and bathrooms) / Non-combustible materials must be used for the false ceilings, cornices, pelmet and decorative panels / No gas pipe is to be enclosed within the false ceilings

when: building kitchen cabinets, dapoh slab or counter top
summary: Kitchen cabinets, dapoh slab and counter tops (on a cement mortar base) need no permit.
conditions: No concrete shelf
Cement mortar base plus tile finishes at most 50mm thick
Owner removes and reinstates fixtures for inspection and maintenance
Do not seal or block the sanitary-duct weephole with carpentry
Gas pipes not embedded in screed or finishes; gas pipe changes need Power Gas approval
Fasteners at most 6mm diameter and 40mm penetration
quote: Construction of dapoh slab/ cabinet with cement mortar base | No | Construction of concrete shelf is not allowed / Total thickness of cement mortar base and tile finishes is not allowed to exceed 50mm

when: carpentry fixed to walls (wardrobes, feature walls, solid timber/mirror wall panels, shelves)
summary: Solid timber/mirror wall panels need no permit; any wall fixing must respect fastener limits, and Ferrolite walls have bolt load and drilling limits.
conditions: Fasteners at most 6mm diameter and 40mm penetration depth
Ferrolite walls: at most 50kg per bolt, bolts at most 50mm long, drill depth about 22mm, no drilling within 200mm below ceilings/beams
Do not cover the kitchen sanitary-duct weephole
Household shelter: see HDB-HS
quote: Solid timber/ mirror wall panel | No | All fasteners/ connectors (e.g. screws, nails, bolts, etc.) used must not exceed 6mm in diameter and 40mm in penetration depth

when: the work is in or on the household shelter (HS)
summary: The household shelter's walls, floor slab, ceiling, steel door and ventilation sleeves must not be tampered with; finishes and fixings inside are tightly restricted (SCDF).
conditions: No hacking or drilling of HS walls/slabs except the permitted 50mm non-metallic inserts
No wall tiles, plaster or rock-stone finish on the internal HS walls
Floor finishes bonded to wet cement mortar only, at most 50mm with screed; no adhesive, no second layer
No cornices inside the HS; no power-driven nails into internal HS walls
Do not modify the HS door or cover its notice, locking bolts or seal
Fixtures inside must be removable within 48 hours
Ventilation openings at least 25% uncovered; 600x600mm access panel under the sleeves if a false ceiling is outside
alternative: Removable fixtures with non-metallic inserts (at most 50mm deep); feature panels only on the external face via spatterdash or power-driven nails.
quote: Like other structural components of the flat, the following features of the HS must not be tampered with during renovation: Reinforced walls / Reinforced floor slab / Ceiling / Steel door

when: the work is not covered by HDB's renovation guide, or its measurements differ from the guide
summary: Works not reflected in the renovation guide, or whose technical details differ from it, need HDB's approval before starting.
quote: Where renovation items are not reflected in the renovation guide or where the measurement and technical details of the proposed work differ from that stated in the renovation guide, you need to seek HDB’s approval before starting the works

when: any renovation work
summary: Every renovation, including works that need no permit, must be done by a contractor from HDB's Directory of Renovation Contractors (DRC); breaches can be fined up to $5,000.
conditions: Permit granted before permit works start
Complete within 3 months (newly completed blocks) or 1 month (existing blocks) of the permit
quote: Engage only contractors from the Directory of Renovation Contractor (DRC) to carry out the renovation, including those works that do not require HDB’s approval

when: any renovation work
summary: General works Mon-Sat 9am-6pm; noisy works (demolishing walls, removing finishes, cutting tiles, heavy drilling) Mon-Fri 9am-5pm only, never on weekends, public holidays or major holiday eves.
conditions: Notify neighbours within 2 units at least 5 days before
At most 2 HDB-approved handheld power tools at a time
Demolition / finish removal at most 3 consecutive days
quote: Restricted renovations such as demolishing of walls, removing wall/ floor finishes, cutting of tiles and heavy and excessive drilling works, etc. can only be carried out between 9:00am and 5:00pm on weekdays only.
